summary.oneLiner: Igarashi Motors India (IMIL) is a Chennai-based precision actuator DC motor maker, established 1996, positioned as a leading global player in actuator motors for automotive applications and a growing supplier of energy-efficient BLDC motor solutions for consumer appliances.
summary.business: IMIL designs and manufactures precision actuator DC motors and motor sub-assemblies for automotive applications, supplying global and domestic Tier-1 suppliers and OEMs. Its automotive range began with Electronic Throttle Control within Engine Air Management and has extended into safety-critical applications (EPB, PLA, GBA, ABS) and body applications (TOCD, seat motors, HRA). Alongside automotive, it makes energy-efficient BLDC motors and driver electronics (ESDM) for the electrical consumer durables / FMEG segment, having entered BLDC ceiling fan motors in 2020.

currentContext.strengths: Leading position in Engine Air Management with an estimated ~13% share of the global engine air management motor market and ~42% domestically (43% share cited in the domestic Passenger Car market)|Installed-base scale and manufacturing experience: ~625 million DC motors populated since 1996 and ~6 million BLDC motor solutions since 2020|Strong parentage - technology development, product expertise, manufacturing practices and global customer engagement support from Igarashi Japan; Igarashi Global is the world leader in TOCD motor applications for passenger cars|Tech-neutral product architecture that works across ICE, Hybrid and BEV platforms (e.g. EPB), insulating the portfolio from powertrain transition|Long-standing customer relationships with global and domestic Tier-1 suppliers and OEMs, with entry into the Korean market adding depth to international presence|Breadth of application portfolio built off one core competence - from EAM into safety-critical (EPB, PLA, GBA, ABS) and body (TOCD, seat, HRA) applications, plus BLDC/ESDM for consumer appliances
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen the core position in automotive DC motors and sub-assemblies while broad-banding the product spectrum into new applications|Diversify beyond Engine Air Management into safety systems (EPB, GBA, PLA, ABS) and body systems (TOCD, seat actuation), building platforms for future growth|Expand automotive motor sub-assembly leadership into seat motor sub-assemblies, molded stator and armature assemblies, and BLDC stator/rotor assemblies for CCH applications|Build ESDM / electronics capability - advanced BLDC driver platforms and controllers for consumer, industrial/domestic, automotive and energy applications, including in-house development of electronic components for the Company's own automotive requirements|Position India as an alternate global sourcing base as OEMs and Tier-1s adopt multi-sourcing to reduce single-region dependence, leveraging the support of parent Igarashi Japan|Deepen OEM and Tier-1 partnerships and reinforce localization, realigning supply chains to meet customer requirements|Enhance manufacturing efficiency through automation and operational excellence, and scale infrastructure and product portfolio|Align the BLDC portfolio with revised BEE 2.0 ceiling-fan energy efficiency norms through advanced driver platforms, improved controllers and smart features|The Company has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture company as on March 31, 2026 (Form AOC-1 Parts A and B are NIL), so capital is deployed within the standalone entity. Dividend is governed by an adopted Dividend Distribution Policy hosted on the Company's website; the Board recommends the payout after holistically considering the relevant circumstances and in line with that policy, and it does not propose to transfer any amount to the general reserve. No loans or guarantees were given during the year; the only investments made were captive renewable-energy tie-ups - Delta Renewable Energy Private Limited (captive solar power consumption) and Navee Green Energy LLP (partnership contribution for captive solar and wind power) - both stated as not related parties. Material related-party dealings with Igarashi Electric Works Limited, Japan are put to members annually for approval and are to be carried out at arm's length and in the ordinary course of business. The Audit Committee oversees hedging protocols, internal financial controls, risk management systems and inter-corporate loans and investments.|Company has undertaken a goal to reduce generation of hazardous waste year on year as a proportion of sales|More than 50% of electricity is consumed from wind energy (green electricity), reducing GHG emissions|Installation of solar panels, solar water heaters and LEDs at various locations for efficient energy management, alongside equipment efficiency improvements that have reduced overall energy intensity|Energy audit conducted, with actions to be taken based on priority/feasibility and allocated budget; energy meters installed in the facility to monitor consumption|Positive engagement with supply chain partners for analyzing Scope-3 emissions|Hazardous waste - oil-soaked waste, epoxy powder waste, gel and varnish - co-processed in cement kilns through a Tamil Nadu State Pollution Control Board approved vendor; bio-medical waste, e-waste, waste oil, spent solvent and empty chemical containers disposed through a TNPCB-approved dismantler|Innovation practices undertaken with customers and suppliers to eliminate the use of hazardous chemicals in products|Water conservation through auto cut-off valves and rainwater use, with water meters installed to analyse non-production consumption; water discharged to the MEPZ-owned common sewage treatment plant and treated water reused for gardening|Company-wide Occupational Health and Safety SOP, with frequent safety audits, awareness sessions, tool box talks and safe-working-practice training for all employees and associates|BLDC fan motors capable of reducing about 50% of energy consumption per motor|Monthly reviews and regular monitoring of legal compliance supported by a Compliance Dashboard software tool|Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers (POSH and Whistle Blower policies), customers and value chain partners, with an Anti-corruption policy overseen by the Audit Committee
currentContext.expansion: The routed text contains no named capex project, capacity number or commissioning timeline. What the Company does describe is capability expansion rather than a plant programme: during FY 2025-26 it commenced commercial production for several new programs, expanded its product portfolio by enhancing DC motor applications and introducing new automotive ESDM applications, and strengthened its manufacturing capabilities for safety applications to serve global Tier-1 customers and OEMs. Entry into the Korean market, with growth in Seat Sub-assembly and EPB Actuator businesses, is described as a landmark addition to its international footprint. Management frames the next phase as scaling infrastructure and product portfolio, enhancing manufacturing efficiency through automation and operational excellence, and diversifying supply chains including localization; no rupee capex outlay or dated project is disclosed in this section.
currentContext.mdna: Moderation in growth and profitability was driven by external factors - geopolitical uncertainty, evolving tariff policies, changes in the USMCA framework, commodity and currency volatility and supply chain disruption - causing higher input costs, logistics challenges and temporary demand softness in certain markets|Commodity cost pass-through mechanisms operate with an inherent timing lag, so input-cost spikes hit margins before recovery|Mitigation levers cited: cost optimization, supplier diversification, streamlined operations and close collaboration with customers and suppliers|Global industry transition towards hybrid engines, higher efficiency systems and increased automation favours manufacturers prioritizing hybridization, software-led platforms and diversified/localized supply chains|Indian passenger vehicle demand supported by rising domestic demand, tax rationalization and localization measures; proactive policies favouring hybrid mobility|Global trade realignment: OEMs and Tier-1s adopting multi-sourcing for risk diversification and supply continuity, positioning India as a credible manufacturing and sourcing hub|BEE 2.0 energy efficiency norms for ceiling fans accelerating the transition towards BLDC-based solutions, creating opportunity in energy-efficient applications|Products validated on global platforms across EAM, Safety, Body, Seat and BLDC systems, which the Company cites as a competitive advantage in winning multi-sourcing share|Management describes the order pipeline as healthy: 'With our internal fundamentals remaining robust and our order pipeline healthy, we are well positioned to capitalize on improving market conditions'|Multiple programs transitioned to production during the year, strengthening execution visibility and growth momentum|A robust pipeline across global and domestic markets alongside a diversified portfolio and regulatory tailwinds|Commercial production started for several new programs during the year

risks.risk: Macro risks and strategic foresight - geo-political developments, changing tariff regimes and trade policy uncertainty
risks.note: Igarashi operates in a dynamic global environment where geo-political developments, changing tariff regimes, trade policy and tariff uncertainties, inflationary pressures, energy crisis and fluctuations in global automotive demand may impact export business and supply chains; mitigation is through diversifying the customer base and export markets, local-for-local supply chain resilience and close monitoring of regulatory developments.

Rapid transition towards vehicle electrification, advanced mobility solutions and evolving customer requirements necessitates continuous product innovation; the Company channels resources into R&D to strengthen BLDC motor technologies and develop motor solutions for next-generation mobility.

risks.risk: Market dynamics and competitive edge - pricing pressure and localization requirements
risks.note: Increasing global competition, pricing pressure, localization requirements and evolving customer sourcing strategies influence market dynamics; addressed by engineering expertise, cost competitiveness, supply-chain re-alignment and expanding presence across global OEMs, new applications and export markets.

risks.risk: Operational excellence and agility - quality benchmarks, supply chain complexity and raw material volatility
risks.note: Rigorous quality benchmarks, intricate supply chain dynamics, raw material price volatility, logistics challenges and workforce adaptation alongside advancing automation; mitigated by strengthening supply chain durability, digital manufacturing and upgrading employee capabilities including FMEA and system validation.

risks.risk: Financial stability and risk hedging - forex, commodity and interest rate exposure
risks.note: Foreign exchange fluctuations, commodity price volatility, interest rate movements and changing global economic conditions may affect financial performance; managed through hedging protocols overseen by the Audit Committee, commodity price pass-through arrangements, working capital optimisation and flexible capital allocation.

Escalating cyber risks, data protection challenges and evolving regulatory requirements for personal data; addressed with robust IT controls, periodic vulnerability assessments, employee awareness programmes and continuous real-time monitoring of critical systems.

risks.risk: Sustainability and ESG leadership - environmental regulation and customer sustainability expectations
risks.note: Environmental regulations, customer sustainability expectations and workplace safety and welfare requirements continue to shape business operations; addressed through energy-efficient operations, responsible resource management, an ESG-compliant supply chain system and regulatory compliance.

Extreme weather events due to climate change pose a physical risk of disruption to operations and to the safety of employees; a contingency plan and trained emergency response team members are in place, with property damage capable of halting operations for a limited time.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
